messages:
maria_support: Hey team — customer ACME reported a spike of 503s since ~08:12 UTC. They see repeated upstream worker failures (503 gateway) on hosted inference API when hitting /v1/generate. Example request-id: req_0a9f3c. They say it started after ~07:50 and affects bursts with longer prompts. Customer is seeing ~20% error rate on retries. attaching sample curl:

curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-live-***" \n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n  -d '{"model":"gptx-large","input":"<~1k token prompt>","max_tokens":1024}'

maria_support: I already escalated and asked for logs; they sent the last few request-ids (req_0a9f3c, req_0a9f8f, req_0aa012). They reported retries sometimes get 500 instead of 503. Customer is pretty upset about lost calls in the analytics pipeline.

sara_ops: Acknowledged. I'm tailing the ingress and worker logs for those request ids. Adding @raj_engineering and @james_infra. Can someone check node health and recent deploys?

deploy-bot: Deploy event: runtime-service v2026.04.11 pushed to hosted-cluster-3 at 07:40 UTC (commit 3f7b2a). No automatic canary enabled (global rollout).

raj_engineering: Noted. First hypothesis: new runtime may have a regression around GPU mem handling for longer context. Asking infra for GPU memory histograms around 07:40-08:20. Also want the container stdout/stderr for the crashed worker.

james_infra: GPU telemetry: saw several nodes in cluster-3 hit >98% GPU memory between 07:45-08:05, with ephemeral spikes to 100% on p100-20gb group. I see OOM events in nvidia-smi logs aligned with the times the customer reported. Also two containers restarted by kube at 07:57 and 08:03 on node gpu-node-172.

sara_ops: Pasting relevant container log excerpt (worker container). Note: truncated for length.

```
[2026-04-11T07:56:58Z] worker pid=4123 tid=140 aborting: std::bad_alloc
[2026-04-11T07:56:58Z] Caught signal 11 (SIGSEGV) at 0x7f8a2c1e2a
[2026-04-11T07:56:58Z] CUDA Error: out of memory during allocation of 2147483648 bytes
[2026-04-11T07:56:58Z] stack trace (most recent call first):
  at inference::kv_cache::allocate (kv_cache.cc:129)
  at runtime::forward::dispatch (forward.cc:412)
  at runtime::serve::handle_request (serve.cc:1023)
  at main (worker_main.cc:78)
[2026-04-11T07:56:58Z] Process killed by OOM-killer (container)
```

james_infra: From kube events: "OOMKilled" for container redwood-worker-4123 on gpu-node-172. dmesg shows: "oom_reaper: reaped process 4123 (worker) total-vm: ... anon-rss: ..." Also seen a CUDA watchdog reset on the node at 07:57:01.

olivia_support: Customer also shared that downgrading context length to ~512 tokens reduces errors significantly. They couldn't reproduce on small prompts. Could be memory growth with context size.

escalation-bot: Incident severity updated to P1-customer-impact. Runbook: start immediate mitigations and triage.

raj_engineering: OK, immediate mitigations we can push: 1) Apply temporary routing rule to steer heavy-context requests for high-traffic customers to a lower memory model-variant (gptx-large-8q) or to dedicated nodes with larger GPUs. 2) Short-term: reduce continuous batching window + per-request max_batch_tokens to limit memory accumulation. 3) Rollback runtime commit 3f7b2a if we confirm the commit introduced the allocation path change.

sara_ops: I've added a temporary GRPC routing rule to move ACME traffic to dedicated-pool-2 (larger GPUs) and disabled continuous batching for their tenant. Pushing config now.

deploy-bot: Routing rule applied for tenant ACME -> dedicated-pool-2 at 08:05 UTC.

maria_support: Customer confirms fewer 503s immediately after routing change. They still see occasional 500s on retries but much better.

raj_engineering: I pulled the runtime changelist for commit 3f7b2a — looks like it modified kv_cache allocation heuristics and a new eager allocation path for long sequences. That change could explain the increased peak allocation. Reproduced locally with a stress test:

```
# repro script (local) -- spawns many concurrent long-context requests
for i in {1..200}; do \n  curl -s -X POST http://localhost:8080/v1/generate -d '{"model":"gptx-large","input":"<1k tokens>","max_tokens":1024}' &
done
```

raj_engineering: On runtime v2026.04.10 (previous), stress test stays stable. On v2026.04.11 (current) I get several segfaults and CUDA OOM logs. I recommend rolling runtime back to v2026.04.10 while we fix allocation heuristics.

james_infra: Preparing node image for rollback target; also increasing soft memory limits and disabling aggressive prefetch on pool nodes as a precaution. ETA ~15 minutes for staged rollback.

sara_ops: Rolling runtime back on hosted-cluster-3 (canary 10% -> 100% if green). Starting canary now.

deploy-bot: Rollback job started: runtime-service -> v2026.04.10 canary on hosted-cluster-3 (10%) at 08:18 UTC.

raj_engineering: Running a post-rollback stress run against canary — no OOMs so far. Observability: GPU mem usage peaks lower due to older kv_cache path.

maria_support: Customer reports error rate dropped to <1% after rollback. They are satisfied for now but asked for root cause explanation and long-term fix plan.

raj_engineering: Root cause summary draft: regression introduced in commit 3f7b2a changed kv_cache eager allocation behavior for long-context inference, causing per-request peak allocations to grow past device memory for certain batch/concurrency combos. This triggered CUDA OOM -> segfault -> container OOMKills. Long-term fix: revise allocation heuristic to cap eager allocations by device-free-memory estimate and fallback to streaming/paging; add unit/integration tests that simulate long-context concurrency; add a guard to reject requests that would exceed safe allocation thresholds with a 429 rather than crash.

james_infra: Follow-ups from infra: add a node-level GPU health check that drains traffic before watchdog reset; increase metric retention for GPU mem trends for longer windows; tune autoscaler to provision spare capacity for memory spikes.

olivia_support: I'll schedule a customer postmortem call for tomorrow and share contengency docs (how to route to dedicated pools and recommended model variants for high-context workloads).

maria_support: Thanks team. Creating an incident ticket and labeling for postmortem. We'll keep this thread open until fixes land.

raj_engineering: I'll submit a PR with the allocation cap + tests, target stable branch. ETA for PR review and staging: 48 hours. After tests pass we'll re-release a patched runtime and roll forward.

sara_ops: Noting runbook updates: 1) Add routing rule pattern for high-context noisy tenants, 2) Add quick rollback checklist for runtime rollouts, 3) Add a quick toggle to disable continuous batching per-tenant.

escalation-bot: Incident marked RESOLVED at 08:26 UTC after rollback and routing mitigation. Follow-up actions: engineers to create PR (raj), infra config changes (james), docs (olivia).

maria_support: Closing loop with customer: sent summary and told them we will follow up with postmortem. They appreciated the quick rollback and routing change.

raj_engineering: Adding one more note — added a synthetic test to CI that spins up 50 concurrent long-context requests against runtime builds to catch this class of regression.

sara_ops: Thanks all. Will file the postmortem and link to this thread.

maria_support: closing thread here.
